marble.name: Division with remainders
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Solve multi-step word problems using the four operations with whole numbers, including interpreting remainders in context; represent with equations using a letter for the unknown; check with estimation
marble.prompt: If you reads 'a school buys 7 boxes of 24 pens and shares them equally between 8 classes', can they work through all the steps and decide sensibly what to do with any remainder?

cluster.summary: Your child is being introduced to multiplication and division as ways of working with equal groups — understanding multiplication as repeated addition and division as sharing equally.

misconceptions: Doing only one step of a multi-step problem, or losing the intermediate result.
Interpreting the remainder wrongly for the context (rounding down the minibus count).
Key-word guessing the operation instead of reasoning from structure.
Not checking reasonableness, so magnitude/step errors go unnoticed.
Writing an equation that doesn't match the problem, or misusing '=' operationally across multiple steps.
representations: Bar model — planning and structuring multi-step problems
Equation with a letter for the unknown (n) — abstracting the plan
Number line / rounding — estimation and reasonableness check
Context frames for remainder interpretation (buses, bags, sharing)
authoredAnswer: First: 6 minibuses (52÷9 = 5 remainder 7; the leftover 7 children still need transport, so round UP). Second: 5 teams (the 7 left over cannot form a full team, so drop the remainder). The teacher watches for the child computing 5 r7 once and then DECIDING what to do with the 7 based on the situation.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: same treatment of the remainder in both problems, wrong in one
wrongAnswers.fix: ask 'what happens to the 7 leftover children in THIS story?' — force the meaning of the remainder in the specific situation to drive the rounding.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: answer left as '5 r7' with no decision about minibuses/teams
wrongAnswers.fix: insist the answer be a sensible real quantity (whole minibuses, whole teams); 'r7' is not an answer to the question asked.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: on the two-step pencil/cost problem, wrong operation or sequence
wrongAnswers.fix: restate as sequential questions and represent with an equation using a letter for the unknown before computing.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: right rounding logic, wrong quotient; estimate (54÷9 = 6) flags it
wrongAnswers.fix: do not reteach interpretation; have the child check with multiplication (6×9 = 54, 5×9 = 45) and estimate.
